title: Angels serve us by office and so know our repentance; nothing shows the dead have that office. Pars Secunda closes
source_text: CI. Sed mirum non est Angelos qui sunt spiritus administratorii in ministerium missi propter eos qui haereditatem capient salutis, cum ex officio nobis adsint, & circa nos versentur, ea scire quae ad nos attinent, & in primis peccatorum poenitentiam & conversionem, cui procurandae ex Dei mandato inserviunt: sed ut jam diximus, munus simile beatis justorum animabus a Deo demandatum esse, ex Dei verbo ostendi non potest. Neque huc facit quod affirmat Christus justos in caelo fore ἰσαγγέλους. Haec enim cum Angelis aequalitas seu similitudo extendi non debet ultra Christi scopum; qui est docere justos post resurrectionem vitam ducturos Angelicam, quatenus hujus vitae necessitatibus & infirmitatibus non amplius subjacebunt, & neque uxorem ducent, neque nuptui dabuntur, ut legenti verba Christi apud Matthaeum planum est. Adde, quod non sequitur, singulos Angelos singulorum hominum cogitationes nosse, & vota percipere, ex eo quod Christus indefinite dicit Angelis gaudium esse propter conversionem unius peccatoris. Sicut vere dicere possumus in Ecclesia Dei gaudium magnum esse, quum peccator unus ad Deum convertitur; Nec tamen inde sequitur singulis qui in Ecclesia sunt, aliorum omnium cogitata, dicta & facta nota esse. Heb. 1. 13.
pass_a_gloss: But it is not wonderful that Angels, who are ministering spirits sent into ministry for those who shall receive the inheritance of salvation, since by office they are present with us, and are occupied about us, know the things which pertain to us, and above all the penitence and conversion of sinners, to procuring which they serve by God's mandate: but, as we have already said, that a similar office has been entrusted by God to the blessed souls of the just cannot be shown from the word of God. Nor does it bear on this what Christ affirms, that the just will be in heaven isangelous. For this equality or likeness with Angels ought not to be extended beyond Christ's scope; which is to teach that the just after the resurrection will lead an Angelic life, inasmuch as they will no longer be subject to the necessities and infirmities of this life, and will neither marry, nor be given in marriage, as is plain to one reading the words of Christ in Matthew. Add that it does not follow that individual Angels know the thoughts of individual men, and perceive their prayers, from the fact that Christ indefinitely says that there is joy to the Angels on account of the conversion of one sinner. Just as we can truly say that there is great joy in the Church of God, when one sinner is converted to God; Yet it does not follow from that, that to each one who is in the Church the thoughts, words and deeds of all the others are known. Hebrews 1:13.
pass_b_english: It is no wonder that angels, who are "ministering spirits sent to serve for the sake of those who will inherit salvation" (Hebrews 1:14), know what concerns us, above all the repentance and conversion of sinners, which they are commanded by God to help bring about. Their office keeps them with us and about us. But, as we have already said, it cannot be shown from God's word that God has entrusted a like office to the blessed souls of the just.

Nor is Christ's saying that the just will be "equal to the angels" in heaven to the point. That equality or likeness to the angels must not be stretched beyond Christ's purpose, which is to teach that after the resurrection the just will live the life of angels, in that they will no longer be subject to the needs and weaknesses of this life and will neither marry nor be given in marriage, as anyone who reads Christ's words in Matthew can see (Matthew 22:30).

Further, when Christ says in general terms that there is joy among the angels over the conversion of one sinner, it does not follow that each angel knows each man's thoughts and hears his prayers. In the same way we can truly say that there is great joy in the Church of God when one sinner turns to God, and yet it does not follow that every member of the Church knows the thoughts, words and deeds of all the others.

choices.english: their office keeps them with us
choices.why: Ex officio grounds the angels' knowledge in their assigned task, which is Le Blanc's whole contrast with the dead.
